Question
========
Like any format, JSON has some limitations. Which of the following is an actual limitation of JSON?

Answerlist
----------
* JSON cannot represent nested or hierarchical data.
* JSON has no built-in way to represent infinity or "not a number" (NaN).
* A JSON text is not valid unless a schema for it has been defined beforehand.
* JSON documents cannot be read by a person without specialized software.


Solution
========
JSON numbers have no representation for special values such as infinity or NaN - if a computation produces one of these, it has to be encoded some other way, for example as a string, before it can be stored in JSON. The other statements are not accurate: JSON handles nested and hierarchical data very naturally, through objects and arrays containing further objects and arrays; a schema is entirely optional and is only used for validation, not for basic validity; and JSON is explicitly designed to be human-readable plain text, no special software required.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* False
* False
